title: Orders report with comprehensions
problem: An admin dashboard needs five small numbers and lists from a list of orders. Implement the five functions in report.py. Each one can be a single return statement using a list, dict or set comprehension, or a generator expression; pick the right kind for each.
requirements: paid_ids: ids of orders whose status is "paid", in input order
cents_by_id: a dict mapping every order id to its cents
customers_with: distinct customers with at least one order of the given status, sorted alphabetically
revenue: total cents of paid orders, 0 if there are none
has_order_over: True if any order's cents is strictly greater than limit
Don't modify the orders or the list
contract:
paid_ids(orders: list[dict]) -> list[int]
cents_by_id(orders: list[dict]) -> dict[int, int]
customers_with(orders: list[dict], status: str) -> list[str]
revenue(orders: list[dict]) -> int
has_order_over(orders: list[dict], limit: int) -> bool
expectedBehavior: For the five sample orders: paid_ids -> [7, 9, 5]; customers_with(orders, 'paid') -> ['ali', 'mina']; revenue -> 2450; has_order_over(orders, 5000) -> False, has_order_over(orders, 4999) -> True.
edgeCases: Empty list for every function (sum of nothing is 0, any of nothing is False)
A customer with several matching orders appears once
The comparison in has_order_over is strict: equal to the limit is not over it
hints: Conceptual: ask what each function returns. An ordered list means a list comprehension. A mapping means a dict comprehension. 'Distinct' means a set, and 'sorted' means sorted() around it. One number or one bool means a generator expression fed to sum or any.
Specific: each order is a dict, so read fields with o["status"] and o["cents"]. Filters go at the end (if ...). A set has no order, so the sorted list must come from sorted(the_set).

Implementation: paid_ids and revenue share the same filter (status == "paid"); one collects ids in [...], the other passes cents to sum(...). customers_with is sorted({... for o in orders if ...}). has_order_over is any(... > limit for o in orders).
evaluation: Each function is a single return with the most fitting comprehension or generator expression
No temporary list built just to be summed or checked with any
Readable: no nested conditionals inside the comprehensions
